source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Genesis 42–45.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves the planted evidence, emphatic silver-cup identification, and fulfillment that establish the accusation’s falsity.
Keeps the claim of divination in the instructed speech without endorsing or denying Joseph’s actual practice.
Keeps the rash death pledge and collective enslavement without softening their proposed penalty.
Retains the source’s apparent assent followed by a changed penalty; the discrepancy is disclosed rather than silently repaired.
Keeps the collective grief and collective return rather than implying they abandon Benjamin.
Retains the emphatic claim as Joseph’s speech without substituting ordinary investigative skill.
Keeps the three questions, attributed divine exposure, and solidarity; guilt is not forced into an admission of cup theft.
Keeps Joseph’s restricted sentence and ironic offer of peace while leaving Benjamin enslaved.
Clarifies the son’s relationship to the speakers and the shared mother while retaining the explicit death report in Judah’s retelling.
Preserves the eye idiom without deciding whether it means simply seeing or protective attention.
Names the likely subject of die in light of 44:30–31, while a note acknowledges the grammatically possible son reading.
Preserves Jacob’s own selective my-wife/two-sons wording rather than correcting it to his whole household.
Keeps Jacob’s inference as reported speech and the emphatic torn-to-pieces expression.
Retains disaster, gray head, Sheol, and the distinct misery term rather than flattening every grief formula.
Keeps the bound-lives image and sentence suspension while explicitly naming both life referents.
Completes the suspended sentence and preserves Judah’s repeated deference and feared responsibility for Jacob’s death.
Recalls Judah’s personal guarantee in 43:9, preserving permanent accountability rather than financial compensation.
Makes the substitution and actual enslavement explicit; servants as court politeness remains distinct from slave as penalty.
